figures.finding: No agreement sets a South African screenwriter's pay: the Writers Guild of South Africa may only recommend rates under the Competition Act, its standard rates and contracts are still being negotiated with the Independent Producers Organisation, and it lobbies for the right to bargain collectively.

value.status: guideline rates only; standard rates and contracts in negotiation with the IPO

figures.applies: South Africa; performance writers for film, television and new media; as of 2026-11-01.

sources.said: According to the South African Competition Act, the Writers Guild of South Africa is not allowed to prescribe rates. The above rates are, therefore, recommended guidelines.

figures.finding: The guild's recommended rates (2019 to 2021, to rise with inflation) put an original feature screenplay with treatment at R200,000-300,000 or 3% of a R1.2-8 million budget, R350,000-500,000 or 2.5% above R8 million, R60,000-80,000 or 6% below R1.2 million and down to R15,000-20,000 or 10% for micro budgets, paid 30% on signing, 20% on the treatment, 30% on the first draft and 20% on the final draft.

value.period: 2019-2021 guideline, expected to escalate with inflation
value.exploitation: usually 1.2% of gross or 0.3% of net profit

figures.applies: South Africa; recommended guidelines, not binding; features.

sources.said: These are the recommended WGSA rates for 2019, which are expected to escalate in accordance with inflation (4.9% in 2018) on a yearly basis. … 30% Advance Payment on Signature of Contract 20% Delivery of Original Treatment 30% Delivery of First Draft Screenplay 20% Delivery of Final Draft Screenplay … Original Screenplay (including Treatment) between R 1,2 million – R 8 million R 200,000.00 – R 300,000.00 (or 3% of overall budget) Top End Screenplay (including Treatment) over R 8 million R 350,000.00 – R 500,000.00 (or 2.5% of overall budget) Low Budget Screenplay (including Treatment) under R 1,2 million R 60,000.00 – R 80,000.00 (or 6% of overall budget) Mini Budget Screenplay (including Treatment) R 200,000.00 – R 500,000.00 R 16,000.00 – R 40,000.00 (or 8% of overall budget) Micro Budget Screenplay (including Treatment) under R 200,000.00 R 15,000.00 – R 20,000.00 (or 10% of overall budget) Non-Original Screenplay/Adaptations (including Treatment) R 180,000.00 - R 220,000.00 … Principal Photography Payment 3-5% of Production Budget Exploitation Contractually agreed upon. Usually 1.2% of gross or 0.3% of net profit.

figures.finding: For television the guild recommends R8,000-12,000 for a 30-minute and R12,000-22,000 for a 60-minute episode of a short-form drama series, R8,000-10,000 for a half-hour soap dialogue episode, R60,000-90,000 a month for a soap head writer (R90,000-120,000 with bible, treatments and script editing on a series) and R60,000-100,000 for a 90-minute TV feature; a telenovela pays at least 20% in advance.
figures.applies: South Africa; recommended guidelines for television, not binding.

sources.said: Including ongoing bible, treatments, and script editing R 90,000.00 – R 120,000.00 Excluding bible and script editing, but inclusive of episode treatments R 60,000.00 – R 80,000.00 … TV Features R 60,000.00 – R 100,000.00 … Short Form Series or Serials (incl. drama and youth R 8,000.00 – R 12,000.00 R 12,000.00 – R 22,000.00 … Head Writer per month R 60,000.00 – R 90,000.00 Storyliner (per full half-hour episode rotating A, B, C storylines among storyliners) R 5,000.00 – R 7,000.00 … Script/Dialogue Writer (half-hour episode) R 8,000.00 – R 10,000.00 … A minimum of 20% of contract price should be paid as an advance before screenwriting begins on a telenovela.

figures.finding: The Writers Guild of South Africa (422 members in March 2023) takes a writer with produced work as a full member for R700 a year, an unproduced writer as a candidate for R500 and a student for R220, with 40% off for over-60s and payment plans; it gives contract advice but has no lawyers.
